sections.title: Letter sound ge
paragraphs: The letter name is (ge) /xe/. Its main sound is heard in (gato) /ˈɡa.to/, which means cat. This letter has three sounds.

sections.title: How to say ge
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Stop the air completely, turn on your voice, then release it. For the second sound, keep a small gap so the air squeezes through smoothly with voice. For the third sound, raise the back of your tongue near the roof and push out voiceless air. Touch your throat to feel it stay still.

sections.title: Spelling rules for ge
paragraphs: After a pause or a nasal consonant before a, o, or u, it sounds like (gato) /ˈɡa.to/ or (tengo) /ˈteŋ.ɡo/. Between vowels or after other sounds before a, o, or u, it softens, as in (amigo) /aˈmi.ɣo/ and (largo) /ˈlaɾ.ɣo/. Before e or i, it makes a rough throat sound, as in (gente) /ˈxen.te/ and (girar) /xiˈɾaɾ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with ge
paragraphs: Do not make a hard stop in words like (amigo) /aˈmi.ɣo/. Let the air glide through softly instead of snapping shut like in go. Before e or i, avoid the soft English sound in gentle. Push the air from the back of your mouth with no voice.
